text:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-mapping tweak rolled yesterday, we’re seeing a regression in short-request p99 from our hosted fleet.

ravi: Saw that in the dashboards. p50 stable but p99 jumped ~2x on smaller inputs. Any obvious hotspots?

emma: I captured a short perf trace on a small prompt (len 32): prefill completes quickly, then decode latency spikes while KV misses spike. Looks like solve-time during kernel handoff is starving KV priming.

alex: Exact numbers from the trace: p99 prefill 28ms -> 30ms, decode p99 95ms -> 210ms, KV miss rate up from 3% -> 18% in the same window.

sophia: That suggests prefill and decode batches are getting conflated and the allocator is choosing a bigger kernel that warms KV in decode but only after handshake. We should try isolating lanes.

mike: Agree. Quick experiment idea: introduce a soft-phase window where prefill batches are allowed to form up to N tokens or T ms, then force a phase-gate so decode batches get their own small kernel path. Could reduce KV thrash.

ravi: Proposed config patch for canary (very conservative):
```yaml
batcher:
  phase_separation:
    enabled: true
    soft_window_ms: 10
    max_tokens_prefill: 64
    decode_token_budget: 8
    preferential_kernel: "small-kernel-v2"
```

emma: Nice. Also add token-budget scaling by queue-length to avoid starving decode when there’s a sudden surge of short requests. E.g. decode_token_budget = max(8, min(32, queue_len*2)).

alex: I ran a quick microbenchmark locally with a synthetic mix (70% short, 30% long). With soft_window_ms=10 and decode_token_budget=8 we got p99 decode down from 210ms -> 120ms and overall cost slightly up (~3%) due to more small-kernel invocations.

sophia: That cost trade-off is ok if latency stabilizes. Can we validate KV miss rate change?

emma: Yes — KV miss rate drops from 18% -> 6% in the microbench. The handshake wait time falls by ~24ms on average.

infra-bot: deploy:canary finished for cluster-us-west-2 at 2026-03-10T14:05Z (sha ab12cd).

mike: Canary graphs look promising for small-rps hosts: p99 decode improved ~35%, tail CPU spikes reduced. But some dedicated-heavy hosts saw throughput dip ~4% under long sequences.

ravi: That implies kernel selection policy still needs tuning: prefer small-kernel for decode-only lanes, but let long-seqs pick large-kernel. We should add a kernel-affinity heuristic keyed by recent sequence length histogram per lane.

alex: Action items:
- short-term: keep canary rolling, increase sample size to 24h. (owner: emma)
- medium: implement token-budget scaler by queue_len and lane-histogram kernel-affinity. (owner: ravi)
- monitor: add KV miss-rate alert (threshold 10% sustained over 5m). (owner: mike)

emma: Filed PERF-3124 with the traces and the microbench results. I'll attach config diffs and the quick flamegraphs.

sophia: If canary holds, let's ship to staging and enable for 10% of production next deploy. Keep rollback plan ready (revert ab12cd).

alex: Thanks everyone. Small follow-up: Ravi, can you post the pseudo-code for the kernel-affinity rule once you have a draft?

ravi: Will do — drafting now, expect a PR by EOD.

emma: Closing loop — pasted the relevant flamegraph link: https://internal-graphs/reports/perf/4315000000-prefill-decode.

mike: Also adding a short logline to the ops runbook on what to watch. If p99 stays >150ms we revert canary.

alex: Great. We'll regroup tomorrow after 24h of canary data. :thumbsup:
